newsitem.title: USA: Mexico election outcome validates rating-Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Mexico election outcome validates rating-Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said Thursday that Mexico's congressional election earlier this month validated its Ba2 foreign currency rating.
"We feel that that the outcome of the elections serves to reinforce and validate the Ba2 rating in terms of a very short-term view," said Mauro Leos, senior analyst at Moody's.
"We still have to wait and see ... if that will translate into an improved political and economic outlook."

Moody's would watch how the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which lost its majority in the lower house of Congress for the first time since 1929, governed in conjunction with the opposition People's Action Party (PAN and Party for the Demorcratic Revolution (PRD).
"We are going to be looking at how well the three parties are able to handle themselves in Congress," Leos said.
Leos said there was always a concern about the potential for the Mexican peso to appreciate in real terms, translating into pressure on the trade accounts and balance of payments.
